references.text: The psalmist asks God to remember him – "Remember me, O Lord, in your favor toward your people" ([ref:Ps 106:4|Psalm 106:4]). The thief on the cross uses a similar prayer when he asks Jesus to remember him, thus showing deep trust in Jesus' power and grace.

Joseph in prison asks the cupbearer: "Remember me" ([ref:Gen 40:14|Genesis 40:14]). The prayer to be remembered by one who has the power to save is a recurring theme in the Bible, reaching its climax in the thief's plea to Jesus.

Jesus' answer to the thief's prayer: "Today you will be with me in Paradise" ([ref:Lk 23:43|Luke 23:43]). Jesus not only remembers him but gives him far more than he asked for – immediate entry into Paradise.

The angel Gabriel announces that Jesus will reign as king forever and ever ([ref:Lk 1:33|Luke 1:33]). The thief acknowledges Jesus' kingship when he says "when you come into your kingdom," confirming what the angels foretold at Jesus' birth.

Jesus tells Pilate: "My kingdom is not of this world" ([ref:Jn 18:36|John 18:36]). The thief understands this and asks to be remembered when Jesus comes into his (heavenly) kingdom, not an earthly one.

Paul speaks of Christ Jesus as the one who "will judge the living and the dead, and at his appearing and his kingdom" ([ref:2 Tim 4:1|2 Timothy 4:1]). The thief's prayer points forward to Jesus' return and the kingdom he will bring to completion.

The context for the thief's prayer is his confession in [ref:Lk 23:40–41|Luke 23:40–41], where he rebukes the other thief, acknowledges his own guilt, and declares Jesus innocent. This repentance and faith form the basis of his prayer.
Jesus as the king who comes into his kingdom and receives the blessed ([ref:Mt 25:31–34|Matthew 25:31–34]). The thief begs this very king to remember him, and Jesus takes him into his kingdom.

God "has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of the Son he loves" ([ref:Col 1:13|Colossians 1:13]). The thief on the cross is the most dramatic example of this transfer – from judgment and death to Christ's kingdom in a single day.

The disciples ask Jesus: "Will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?" ([ref:Acts 1:6–7|Acts 1:6–7]). The thief's prayer shows an expectation of Jesus' future kingdom, an expectation the disciples also had, but the thief expresses it in faith and humility.

"The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever" ([ref:Rev 11:15|Revelation 11:15]). The thief's prayer to be remembered "when you come into your kingdom" points toward the final fulfillment of Christ's kingship.
